pitch_detail.notes: Starts up a blank slab to a first bolt about 8 m off the ground, then to a second bolt on the left side of the arch. Flakes lead left to a ledge system with two tiny trees, then slabs and right-facing flakes trend right past one more bolt to the belay. Mixed bolts and gear.

Gear and a piton at the start, then a right-trending crack that passes right of an overhang. Step left to another piton and continue more directly up the slab on flakes and an undercling past four bolts to a narrow stance.
Drifts left then right past one bolt each, with flakes and an undercling taking adequate gear, and one more bolt near the end. A small stance under the right side of an overlap holds the anchor.
Go straight up, passing the overlap on its right, then climb a slabby section with flake features. The belay hangs from the underside of an overlap and is hard to spot.

Step left a few metres and angle left for about 15 m, then climb more directly up the slab past three bolts and a corner weakness onto easier slab. Pass the last overlap on its left side and trend right to a sloping ledge.
Easy slab, 5.1 at most, with a lone bolt right of a shallow grassy gully. The anchor sits on a block where the slab ends; steep grass then leads up to a large meadow.

review.changed: Wrote 6 pitches with grades, lengths, bolt counts and anchors as stated. P6 grade given as 5.1 (stated as 5.1 to 4th class). Piton counts not captured as a field. Rappelling the route with two 60 m ropes is mentioned but no stations, so no rappel table; walking off is the preferred descent.

pitch_detail.notes: From the right side of the wide sloping ledge, follow diagonal flakes trending right to a small left-facing corner about 45 m up. Clip a bolt above it and cross a smooth slab left to a gentle dish for the belay.
Move left across a slab to a shallow right-facing corner and flake system, then follow a double orange dike past three bolts to a set of overlaps. Cross the first overlap and belay below the second.

Above the anchor, one bolt protects the move past the first overlap, then the line angles right past a second bolt along the end of another overlap. Above it, head back left past a third bolt to a stance under a larger overlap.
Traverse right around the overlap, then go up a vertical line on steeper featured slab past four bolts. The last 15 m drift right toward a ledge that doubles as a descent stance.
Cross a small overlap and trend right on featured slab, three bolts in all, aiming for a left-facing corner standing over a small tree. The corner ends at a comfortable ledge.

Go up the slab past a bolt toward a slabby arete, then follow the arete past two bolts to easier ground. Work up and right via left-facing cracks and flakes, traverse left under a dark overlap to a dark right-facing corner, then step left onto a clean wall and follow vertical cracks up and left to a good ledge.

Lower-angle slab trending right with a bolt, ending at the right side of a big overlap beneath a tree-covered patch. Then up and left past one more bolt to a right-facing corner system; a good hand crack lies in it, and the ledge is just right of the corner under a steep wall.

Step left off the stance and keep following the corner system, staying just left of an arete, until the angle relents. Easy slab and cracks go straight up right of a loose gully and the trees to a sloping ledge under an overhanging wall.

review.changed: Wrote all 8 pitches with stated grades, lengths, bolt counts and anchors. No rappel stations given.

pitch_detail.notes: Leave the cave via its right side, reach a ledge holding a small tree, and continue up from its right end with good protection. Easy slab ends on a wide ledge littered with boulders. The wet, awkward gully scramble is an alternative way to the same ledge.

Move the belay about 7 m to the right so you stand beneath a right-facing corner; one bolt is visible well above. Climb the corner to two widely spaced bolts, then angle left under a leaning roof. Pulling its far end gives a stance with a hidden bolt, then a tricky step leads into another roof where a last bolt marks the crux before a good ledge.
A tricky move off the belay gains an open-book corner. Climb through a bulge to a bolt and stance, then head up and right, run out, to stacked pillars and a belay under a roof.

Traverse left along a wide, dirty crack toward a cave, then step right onto blocky ground and climb the slab above past two bolts. A thin crack with a pin leads to technical moves, another bolt and a big flake before a good ledge.
Follow the left-facing corner beneath the big chockstone, then move left onto face cracks. A bulge climbed back to the right leads to a good ledge.
Carry on up the left-facing corner, then shift right into a second one. It tops out on a big ledge where the belay is a bolt plus a sling. A scramble gets you to the summit.

review.changed: Wrote 6 pitches with stated grades and lengths; crux flagged on P2 (5.11b, the top pitch grade). Descent is 6 single-rope rappels but stations are not listed, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Follow a decomposing crack to the roof, move right, then make punchy moves over the roof to a semi-hanging bolted belay. Four bolts protect it. Originally rated 5.11d.

Underclings and crimps pull leftward out of the huge roof to a good stance. Easier ground then works back right to a bolted ledge belay. Gear is hard to spot and place in the cramped roof. Originally rated 5.12a.

Above the belay, a steep flake-crack faces left; follow it, step left on a ledge to a second crack, climb that, then step right onto the next ledge. A blocky crack and protruding buttress continue to bolts at the right edge of a hanging slab.

Work left and a touch down along the edge of the hanging slab, with one piece of gear and three bolts. Reach the airy arete, climb up past one more bolt, then follow a weakness left across an exposed wall to a big ledge with bolted anchors. Holds here crumble, which is where most of the grade comes from.
Take the central crack of three parallel ones (the left one by the arete is a harder, separate line at 5.11+). It ends at bolts under the ridge crest.

review.changed: Wrote 5 pitches with stated grades; no lengths stated. P4 grade given as 5.10d (text says 5.10, rated 5.10d). Rappel stations described only loosely (4 raps, partially located), so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: A 30 m ice pitch with a thin top-out.
Ice with chimney climbing, a small ice cave and thin ice higher up.

rappel_detail.notes: Rap from trees; keep the rope and gear clear of soot left by the burn.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches; very brief source. Rappel table written from the two stations listed.

pitch_detail.notes: Up a chimney with a big chockstone, using good face holds on its side, then cut left out of it when possible at the crux. A bench leads on; go straight up thin cracks to a belay at large boulders. The steepest pitch and no harder than 5.8.
Scramble over the large boulders and pick a line up the headwall. Can be split in two for rope drag but one pitch to the big flat area above the headwall is workable.
Downclimb a notch toward the summit, climb back up to the ridgeline and go straight to the top.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches; only P1 has a grade (5.8 at most). Rappel notes are a general description (down-lead then two full-length rappels with a tagline), not stations, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Scramble to a grassy ledge below paired cracks and climb them past some blocks, then right to an obvious left-facing corner leading to a tree. Past the tree you can stem directly up at 5.8 or take thin cracks to the left on small gear at 5.10a. A slanted tree ledge holds the belay.
Easy ground follows a slanted left-facing corner, then a fun layback gains a wide flaring chimney. The belay is a niche beneath a thin seam directly overhead.

Follow the slab seam toward a menacing left-facing roof. The belay is a horn where a thin finger crack starts, though you can extend to small ledges under the roof. A variation leaves the crack after 20 m with a bold step left onto a crystal knob and thin crack at 5.10a, then needs care with precarious blocks near the belay.
Stay on the same crack to a comfortable ledge under the roof, next to a crystal pocket.

The best pitch. Climb the sloping roof feature up into a steep, twice-overlapped corner. Hand jams change to fingerlocks over the first, and wild stemming with a ringlock passes the second, which is the crux. The crack eases above to a stance.
Wander up good rock to a grassy ledge right of a large white gully.

Traverse left into the white gully and follow a left-facing corner on its right side, trending left to a right-facing corner by a big black ridge. After a stance, low fifth-class scrambling reaches the summit ridge.
Pick a way around big loose blocks to the summit ridge.

review.changed: Wrote 7 pitches plus the P8-10 summit-ridge section as one entry. Pitch lengths and grades as stated; P1 and P3 alternates in notes.
review.other_findings: Stored pitch count 7; text counts 10 including the ridge section.

pitch_detail.notes: Blocky orange granite angling slightly right up an obvious weakness to a good ledge with solid gear.
Easy ground (about 5.4) angles up and left to a short steep corner, where the 5.10c moves are. A small ledge above takes good gear.
Straight up to a terrace.
Walk the belay right to the base of an obvious grey dike.

The grey dike offers moves from vertical to slightly overhanging. Build the belay on good gear to the left, in the steep wall above. Loose boulders and dirt around to the right allow a scramble to the top of the pitch.
Climb the vertical wall on the left to the crest and follow it up to where large blocks make it easier. Belay on a good ledge just above.
Go right and up through blocks toward a big dark corner, then up the corner on good gear to a stance.
Continue up left, then straight, over blocky terrain toward the summit to a small ledge with good gear.
Easy blocky rock straight to the summit using a full rope. A crack near the top takes good gear and holds a rappel anchor.

review.changed: Wrote 9 pitches with stated grades and lengths. Descent is four 60 m rappels without individual stations, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Diagonal up left along natural features and great holds to a small ledge with excellent gear.
Keep going up left into a chimney/gully feature and a v-crack, then follow the right-angling v-crack to a small ledge with good gear.

Up and right into an obvious right-facing corner capped by a small roof, with a splitter 10c finger crack above leading into a chimney. Exit the chimney to the left and belay on a sloping ledge. Gear in a crack on the left needs a nut tool to clear.
Shift the belay left and up to a large comfortable ledge with great gear.
Two splitter cracks side by side lead straight up to a slabby right-facing corner. Keep going on broken, ledgy ground to a comfortable stance.
Keep left toward the summit ridge, reaching it at the top of a loose broken gully on the left. Belay from blocks on the ridge crest.

review.changed: Wrote 6 pitches with stated grades and lengths. Descent is a hike, no rappels.

pitch_detail.notes: Diagonal up left along natural features and great holds to a small ledge with excellent gear.
Continue left into a chimney/gully feature and a v-crack, then follow the right-angling v-crack to a small ledge with good gear.
Go up an arete for about 15 ft to a ledge allowing a hard traverse left. Cracks in the wall ahead take good gear. Descend slightly into a right-facing corner and follow it to a nice ledge.
Straight up large blocks to a crack in the face that leads to a great ledge with a gear belay. This is where the route rejoins the harder neighbouring line.
Twin splitter cracks go straight up to a slabby right-facing corner, then continue into broken ledgy ground to a comfortable stance.
Stay left, heading for the summit ridge via the top of a loose, broken gully on the left. Belay on blocks on the ridge.

review.changed: Wrote 6 pitches with stated grades and lengths; P4 at 5.8+ is the route's top grade. Descent is a hike.

pitch_detail.notes: Easy 5.7 rock leads directly to a ledge with trees. Push through the krummholz to a good crack in the back wall on the left, and belay from a tree.
Straight up a good crack/corner using crack technique and stemming to a big ledge. Belay from a tree or gear.

A crack goes up from the left end of the ledge. Gear and jams are good, though some lichen is present. A small ledge is reached, then 5.7 ground continues to the top of the wall, where a boulder or gear forms the belay.

review.changed: Wrote 3 pitches with stated grades and lengths. Descent is one or two double-rope rappels, without stations listed, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep snow to a short AI2 step. Set up the belay below the next steep section wherever the ice is good enough.
Climb the near-vertical step for about 15 m until it eases, then belay at the next flow of ice. Gear was poor in the steep part, mostly thin crusted 85-degree snow.
Go about 5 m left and up a steep snow slope, which gets to 70 degrees in places. Thin trees are the only protection, via slings. The belay is under the next steep ice step.

Two options from the belay: a gentler snow and neve slope with ice to the left (thin veneers over rock) or a steeper right-hand line. The right was climbed, more vertical snice than alpine ice. The hard section is about 20 m, then it eases to good neve. Stretch the rope to reach decent ice on the left.
Easiest pitch: good neve at 45 degrees to a tree belay.
Going left from the previous belay looks like good neve and is the better choice. The line climbed went straight up steep 70-degree snow and trees to a tree belay below a good ice flow.
About 30 m of solid alpine ice, with no gear for the first 10 m and good screws after. As it eases, climb to the end of the rope and build an ice anchor.
More alpine ice at AI2 easing to 50-degree neve. Stretch the rope and belay off a tree.

Where to go is hard to read in the dark: straight up may be a rowdy snow pitch or an easy snow romp, so the line went right through trees up steep snow. A full pitch reaches terrain easing to under 30 degrees; belay from a tree.

review.changed: Wrote 9 pitches; lengths as stated, grades only where given. Crux flagged on P4 as named. No rappels (walk off over the ridge).

pitch_detail.notes: Easy unprotected corner and slab on good rock for about 15 m, up and over a small bush, then across a ledge to a belay in a right-facing corner below an obvious hand crack.
Continue up the right-facing corner for about 20 m to an excellent hand crack, then follow the crack another 25 m. The belay ledge sits at the foot of a second right-facing corner.
Climb the corner until the rock worsens at about 10 m, cross the slab right to a tree, then a crumbly groove up and left to a short chimney. Pass shrubs to a belay at a crack that takes a .75 cam.
Move left a couple of metres on the ledge, climb a thin crack with nice features and a short crux, then cracks and chimneys with some poor rock to a big ledge. Save a number 3 cam for here.

review.changed: Wrote 4 pitches with stated grades and lengths. Summit scramble (4th class) not a pitch. No rappels.

pitch_detail.notes: Traverse across the dip to a good ledge with a bolt. Then walk west about 80 m before climbing.
Climb up where the slab angle lessens; many variations exist and protection is generally adequate.
More slab climbing up to a broken ledge. Depending on the line chosen, you might simul-climb or add a pitch to reach it.
Follow the broken ledge up and to climber's right through cedars, then cracks to a large block. Pass it on the left to a good ledge.
Scramble up, then follow a dihedral left. Step onto it where it thins to reach a ledge by some trees. A forest hike of about 30 minutes leads to the summit.

review.changed: Source pitches are unlabelled; wrote 5 in order (stored count 6). P1 length is the short 5 m traverse. Descent mostly reverses the route with some downclimbing and optional rappels, no stations listed.

pitch_detail.notes: Long 5.7 opener on mostly bolted belays.
The bolt-protected crux of the route.
Shorter 5.6 pitch.
Long 5.6 pitch, the longest on the route, so a 70 m rope is needed.
Short easy pitch.
Long 5.8 pitch.
Moderate climbing at 5.5.
A 5.8 pitch near the top.
Easy full-length pitch.
Fourth-class finish.

review.changed: Wrote 10 pitches with grades and lengths only; the source gives no per-pitch description, so notes are brief. Belays are mostly bolted, otherwise trees or boulders to sling.

pitch_detail.notes: A 35 m crack reaches a wide ledge with trees and a fixed anchor.

Climb a broken finger/hand crack up and slightly right for about 10 m to a large alcove, then out its left side (stemming and chimneying make it easier without a pack). Belay on a small ledge above the alcove, kinder for a struggling second, or follow cracks up and slightly right to another anchor. Longer runners help.
Follow the continuous crack system to a treed ledge with an anchor.
Leaving the anchor takes an awkward squirm up a squeeze on the left. About 30 m of enjoyable cracks follow to the top.

review.changed: Wrote 4 pitches. Rappel is the route with a 70 m rope, no station list, so no rappel table.

pitch_detail.notes: A crack and corner trending right take you to a belay tucked behind a big detached block.
Continue up the ramp as it thins into a roof. From the right end of it, step right on face holds to a thin, cruxy crack, then belay on a ledge.
A long pitch. Start with a short awkward offwidth to reach a left-trending diagonal crack and follow it across the face.
Leave the ledge toward the left on easy ground, then stem a right-leaning, right-facing corner and pull its roof. Easier ledges above lead to a belay ledge.
Flakes and a short corner lead up to a higher ledge. Many parties link it with the next pitch into one long lead.
Step down and right, then take a prominent diagonal hand crack leaning right all the way to the summit ridge.

review.changed: Wrote 6 pitches (P5 and P6 separated, source allows them as one). Grades and lengths as stated.

pitch_detail.notes: Steep snow leads to one pitch of WI4, then a short traverse right to the base of the main flow.
WI5 ice to the top over the remaining pitches.

review.changed: Wrote P1 and a combined P2-4 entry; the source does not separate the upper pitches. No lengths. Rappels are described only as rappel the route.

pitch_detail.notes: Starts with a steep wide pillar and belays on a bench at the top, over 60 m up.
Steepening ice above the ledge finishing below the rock headwall, where ice pours out of the wall. It can form as a massive hollow tube with thin ice, so be wary of hollow-sounding ice.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches with no per-pitch grades; headline is WI5.

pitch_detail.notes: Moderate ice early on goes bad after about 35 m. Steep snice follows, then a rising traverse right over snow-dusted rock to the foot of a lovely ice-filled groove. The final 10 m or so are poor quality.
Steep, sustained ice up the groove to the top.

review.changed: Wrote 2 pitches; no per-pitch grades or other lengths. Rappel the route, no stations listed.
